rv.q: But how often do you get a West End play that's intelligent, funny and puts contemporary mid-life women centre stage?
This sounds like a timely and heartfelt comedy of misunderstanding, not to say breakdown, between the generations.
Jumpy, transferred to the Duke of York’s from the Royal Court, does all three and is just the sort of original, daring new play that the West End badly needs.
But it is still, thanks in large part to Greig, a play well worth catching.

cn.t: April de Angelis's smart, thought-provoking comedy about female mid-life crisis brings original daring to the West End, anchored by Tamsin Greig's affecting performance in Nina Raine's sparky production.
